## TL;DR

Updated launchd detection so a detached, hand-started RepoOS server parented by pid 1 can be classified as hand-run after launchd’s accessible domains have been searched successfully and no matching job was found. If domain inspection fails, detection remains uncertain and restart refuses rather than guessing. The CLI now also refuses by default while engineers or checks are active; `--force` is the explicit override, while `--when-idle` continues to wait. Updated CLI documentation and added a fake-process-table test for the nohup/pid-1 case.

The targeted test files passed (34 tests). The first scoped RepoOS check found formatting drift; after `bun run fmt`, the requested scoped RepoOS check passed, including build, 122 changed-path test files, UI smoke, and the user-docs build.

## Work and rationale

The investigation began in `src/core/server-restart.ts`, `src/core/supervisor-detect.ts`, their tests, `src/commands/restart.ts`, and the restart section of `user-docs/cli.md`. The implementation already had a hand-run restart path: it verifies that the located PID serves this repository, captures restart flags before stopping it, waits for the old PID to exit, launches a replacement, and confirms the new PID and version through health polling. This meant the reported refusal happened earlier, during supervisor classification, rather than in the respawn code.

On macOS, the detector checked `launchctl list` and then attempted to inspect the system and applicable GUI domains. If no row matched and the server’s parent was pid 1, it returned `uncertain`. Detached commands such as a nohup-started `repoos serve` are also reparented to pid 1, so parentage alone could not justify refusal once successful domain searches had found no owner. The code now records whether a domain lookup failed. A pid-1-parented process with no matching launchd row is classified as unsupervised only when the accessible domain lookups succeeded. Failed domain lookups preserve the uncertain result; unreadable parentage and failed `launchctl list` remain conservative failures too. Detection still follows the normal external or managed-service paths when it finds a matching launchd label.

A new test injects command outputs for an empty launchd list, successful empty domain inspection, and PPID 1. The existing tests continue to cover the uncertain case when domain inspection fails, a launchd service row, and an unreadable parent. Together these cases make the PID table and supervisor evidence deterministic without signaling any machine process.

The CLI now checks `/api/update-status` before a normal restart and refuses when engineers or checks are active. `--force` bypasses that guard. `--when-idle` retains its wait loop. The usage documentation describes those choices and the hand-run process behavior. No new runtime dependency was introduced.

## Approaches tried

I first traced the current behavior from the task description through `classifyRestartPath` and into `detectDarwinSupervisor`. The restart tests already used injected locate, health, ownership, stop, spawn, and wait functions, and the supervisor tests injected an `execFile` fake. I used the existing fake-table seam rather than attempting to start or stop a live service.

I ran the two directly relevant Vitest files with `bunx vitest run src/core/supervisor-detect.test.ts src/core/server-restart.test.ts`; both files passed, 34 tests total. I also attempted `bun run test --` with those file paths, but this repository’s wrapper does not treat that syntax as a Vitest path filter. It reported “No test files found” for the requested paths while running the wrapper’s boot-timing pass. The direct Vitest invocation was the valid focused result.

I ran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. The remote build ran, but the check reported a formatter failure; `bun run fmt` has since formatted the tree. After formatting, the scoped RepoOS check passed. It completed the build, changed-path tests, UI smoke, rendered contrast audit, and user-docs build.

## Challenges and blockers

The task asks for a live reproduction using a nohup-started server. This is a managed RepoOS task session, whose local instructions prohibit launching `repoos serve` directly; the task’s safety note also prohibits killing a process unless it is verified to serve this project root. I did not launch or terminate any live server and therefore cannot claim that live reproduction or end-to-end restart was observed. The behavior was reproduced in the fake process table: PPID 1 plus no launchd row was the former unconditional refusal, and successful domain inspection now classifies that case as hand-run.

The distinction is deliberately scoped to successful supervisor discovery. When a domain cannot be inspected, a missing row is not proof that the process is unsupervised; the result remains uncertain and restart does not signal it. Linux systemd behavior is unchanged by this code change. The new CLI activity check uses the status endpoint already used by `--when-idle` and fails closed if that endpoint cannot confirm activity state.

## Key learnings

A detached process’s parent PID is not enough to infer ownership. In particular, pid 1 can own reparented children after their original shell exits, so the launchd query result must be evaluated together with whether the relevant domains were actually inspectable. Tests should represent both a successful negative lookup and an incomplete lookup; those outcomes have different safety implications.

The existing restart flow already preserved the port, host, recorded flags, and old/new version reporting once a process was classified as hand-run. The defect was the classifier’s treatment of a common nohup process shape. Focused fake-process tests are the safe way to exercise this classification in a managed environment; a live restart still needs an authorized human environment to observe directly.
